sentences.text: Silvisaurus is a nodosaurid ankylosaur whose name combines Latin for woodland and Greek for lizard, reflecting its likely habitat in a densely forested area.
The skull measures 33 cm in length and 25 cm in width, while the lower jaw contains at least twenty-five teeth, with each upper jaw bone holding between eight and nine teeth.
Large air passages in the head suggest the animal may have produced loud vocalizations for communication.
Teeth at the front of the jaw suggest Silvisaurus was a relatively primitive nodosaurid compared to later forms with beaks.
The species was discovered in the 1950s by Kansas rancher Warren W. Condray, whose help recovered the skeleton in July 1955, before Theodore H. Eaton Jr. formally described and named it in 1960.

The species name honors the rancher who discovered the fossil, which was found in the Terra Cotta Clay Member of the Dakota Formation in Kansas as an incomplete skeleton including the skull, neck, back, tail, and leg bones alongside disarticulated armor plates and spikes, though the fossil condition was poor due to exposure in a dry riverbed and damage from cattle.
Silvisaurus likely possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail in addition to standard armor plates.
Silvisaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 113 to 105 million years ago, in what is now North America, although the time range is also estimated from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
It is debated whether Silvisaurus possessed bony spines on its shoulders and tail.
